text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- German Trade Union Federation (DGB) states its commitment to a "socially regulated" market economy.
- Deutsche Telekom sets share price at 28.5 marks.
- Member of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats gains most votes in first round of elections for mayor of Mainz.
- Medium-sized manufacturing companies were unable to increase income in 1995, survey from IKB Deutsche Industriebank says.
HANDELSBLATT
- Around 1.9 million private investors take part in Deutsche Telekom flotation.
- German regional states and local councils all plan to reduce budget deficits to help Germany meet the Maastricht criteria for Europe's planned single currency.
- Car traffic in Europe will increase significantly between now and 2005, Ifo institute says.
- Negotiators report progress in sick pay talks in chemical industry.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Kohl criticises employers for not doing enough to help fight unemployment, Sueddeutsche Zeitung has learned.
- President Roman Herzog says he will not tread softly on human rights during state visit to China.
- Deutsche Telekom flotation should raise 20 billion marks for the company.
DIE WELT
- Telekom share price lower than expected.
- Finance Minister Theo Waigel speaks out against idea of forming "grand coalition" with Social Democrats (SPD).
- SPD leader Oskar Lafontaine says party will keep all its options open until election year 1998.
- Health Minister Horst Seehofer calls on doctors to cut spending on medicines.
